families.name: FEAR
families.description: Title tries to scare or worry the viewer: threats, danger, doom, loss, worst-case outcomes.

families.name: CURIOSITY
families.description: Title withholds a key fact, answer or outcome so the viewer must click to find out; teasing, mystery, secrets, reveals.
labels: “THEY DON'T WANT YOU TO KNOW” FRAMING

families.name: EXAGGERATION
families.description: Title inflates importance, scale, novelty or stakes: hyperbole, superlatives, world-changing or shocking claims, dramatic verbs like destroyed/killed/dead.

families.name: URGENCY
families.description: Title pressures the viewer to act or watch right now: deadlines, last chance, breaking news, act-now, don't-wait.

families.name: SCARCITY
families.description: Title implies something is limited, rare, exclusive or invite-only.

families.name: FOMO / TREND PRESSURE
families.description: Title suggests everyone is doing, using or talking about something and the viewer will be left behind; trends, bandwagon, hijacking a news moment.

families.name: AUTHORITY
families.description: Title leans on experts, celebrities, institutions, credentials or famous names to seem credible.

families.name: CERTAINTY
families.description: Title states something with unjustified certainty: absolutes, guarantees, predictions or opinions presented as fact.

families.name: MISLEADING FRAMING
families.description: Title frames facts in a slanted way: omitting context or caveats, unfair comparisons, misleading statistics, oversimplifying, false balance.

families.name: VAGUE CLAIM
families.description: Title makes claims that are vague, unverifiable or hand-wavy: weasel words, empty superlatives, insinuation, vague enemies or promises.

families.name: FALSE DICHOTOMY / FALLACIES
families.description: Title relies on a logical fallacy or rhetorical trick: false dichotomy, straw man, slippery slope, whataboutism, loaded question.

families.name: ANGER
families.description: Title tries to make the viewer angry or outraged, or is itself hostile: rage bait, drama, mockery, shaming, callouts, dunking.

families.name: POLARIZATION
families.description: Title divides people into us versus them: tribalism, enemies, scapegoats, identity threats, conspiracy, persecution.

families.name: EMOTIONAL APPEAL
families.description: Title aims mainly at a non-hostile, non-fear emotion: guilt, pity, hope, nostalgia, awe, envy, belonging, love, reassurance.

families.name: STATUS APPEAL
families.description: Title sells prestige, wealth, success, beauty, power or a desirable identity, or triggers status comparison.

families.name: GREED
families.description: Title promises money, profit or financial freedom, or uses pricing psychology: get-rich-quick, passive income, bargains, discounts, free bonuses.

families.name: EASY-SOLUTION PROMISE
families.description: Title promises a fast, easy or secret way to get a result: quick fixes, one-trick solutions, hacks, formulas, transformations.

families.name: DIRECT COMMAND
families.description: Title tells the viewer what to do or uses behavioral-economics nudges: commands, calls to action, commitment, reciprocity, anchoring, loss or gain framing.

families.name: CLICKBAIT / ENGAGEMENT BAIT
families.description: Title or wording exists mainly to farm engagement: asks for likes, comments, shares or subscribes, or hooks the viewer to keep watching, watch till the end or watch a series.

families.name: PERSONALIZATION
families.description: Title speaks directly to the viewer with 'you': direct address, personal warnings, promises or challenges, you're-doing-it-wrong, stop-doing-X.
labels: “IF YOU ARE X, WATCH THIS” FRAMING

families.name: CONTRARIAN BAIT
families.description: Title sets itself against the mainstream or experts: hot takes, unpopular opinions, myth-busting, cover-ups, suppressed truth, censorship.

families.name: SOCIAL PROOF
families.description: Title points to numbers, testimonials, ratings, case studies or other people's use or adoption as evidence.

families.name: TRUST SIGNALING
families.description: Title performs honesty, authenticity or friendship to earn trust: no-BS, brutally honest, behind-the-scenes, vulnerability, personal stories.

families.name: SEX APPEAL / LIFE ANXIETIES
families.description: Title uses attraction, romance or body image, or plays on a specific life anxiety: aging, health, fitness, career, money, relationships, parenting.

families.name: CUTE / HUMOR / SPECTACLE
families.description: Title sells entertainment value: cute, funny, absurd, cringe, chaotic or spectacular content, disasters, and aspirational 'porn' (wealth, luxury, productivity, tech).

families.name: NOVELTY
families.description: Title sells something new, first, leaked or experimental: scoops, breaking news, extreme tests, challenges, stunts, 'I tried X' or 'I spent X' formats.

families.name: BRAND WAR / CONFLICT
families.description: Title stages a rivalry: product versus product, platform or brand wars, generational, gender, class, culture or profession conflict.

families.name: NEGATIVITY BIAS
families.description: Title dwells on bad news, failure, scandal, betrayal, corruption, downfall, collapse or backlash.

families.name: POSITIVE SPIN / PROMOTION
families.description: Title spins an image or sells something: PR, reputation management, ads disguised as content, sales pitches, upsells, self or cross promotion.

families.name: FALSE CONSENSUS / MANUFACTURED
families.description: Title suggests consensus, popularity, controversy, outrage, demand or mystery that looks staged or manufactured rather than real.

families.name: SOURCE LAUNDERING
families.description: Title distorts where a claim comes from or what someone said: laundered claims, quote mining, distorted headlines, misattribution, out-of-context quotes.

families.name: FALSE EXPERTISE / WASHING
families.description: Title fakes or inflates expertise, or borrows the prestige of science, tech, AI, green or health language to seem legitimate.

families.name: CONFIRMATION BAIT
families.description: Title flatters what the viewer already believes: belief or worldview validation, reinforcing biases and stereotypes, echo chamber appeal, victimhood or superiority validation.

families.name: NEUTRAL / INFORMATIONAL
families.description: Title plainly describes the content with no notable persuasion tactic: educational, news, review, tutorial, documentary, commentary, plain entertainment or personal experience.

descriptions.CURIOSITY GAP: Teases something interesting but omits the key fact, so the viewer must click to learn it.
descriptions.INFORMATION GAP: Signals that the video contains information the viewer lacks, without saying what it is.
descriptions.OPEN LOOP: Starts a story or claim in the title and leaves it unresolved.
descriptions.CLIFFHANGER: Ends on a dramatic, unresolved moment.
descriptions.WITHHELD ANSWER: Poses or implies a question and hides its answer.
descriptions.WITHHELD OUTCOME: Describes an event or attempt but hides how it turned out.
descriptions.VAGUE PRONOUN: Uses 'this', 'it', 'he', 'she' or 'they' without saying who or what.
descriptions.VAGUE SUBJECT: Never names the actual subject of the video.
descriptions.QUESTION BAIT: The title is a provocative question designed to be answered by clicking.
descriptions.SECRET KNOWLEDGE: Promises knowledge that supposedly only a few people have.
descriptions.FORBIDDEN KNOWLEDGE: Promises knowledge that is supposedly banned, hidden or dangerous to know.
descriptions.INSIDER KNOWLEDGE: Promises knowledge from someone who worked inside an industry or organization.
descriptions.EXPOSE FRAMING: Presents the video as uncovering wrongdoing or something hidden.
descriptions.HYPERBOLE: Extreme overstatement that is obviously not literally true.
descriptions.SENSATIONALISM: Presents ordinary events in a shocking or lurid way.
descriptions.OVERHYPE: Builds excessive excitement around something that is unlikely to live up to it.
descriptions.OVERPROMISE: Promises a result or payoff the content is unlikely to deliver.
descriptions.STAKES INFLATION: Makes what is at stake sound far bigger than it is.
descriptions.“X IS DEAD” FRAMING: Declares something is dead, finished or obsolete.
descriptions.“X DESTROYED Y” FRAMING: Uses destroyed, obliterated, humiliated or similar violent verbs for a mild outcome.
descriptions.MANUFACTURED URGENCY: Creates a false need to act or watch right now.
descriptions.MANUFACTURED SCARCITY: Suggests something is running out or limited when it is not.
descriptions.BREAKING-NEWS URGENCY: Uses 'breaking' or 'just happened' language to force immediate attention.
descriptions.EARLY-MOVER PRESSURE: Says people who act first will win and latecomers will lose.
descriptions.EXCLUSIVITY: Frames the content or product as available only to a select few.
descriptions.TREND HIJACKING: Attaches an unrelated video to a popular trend to borrow attention.
descriptions.NEWSJACKING: Attaches an unrelated video to a current news story to borrow attention.
descriptions.NAME-DROPPING: Mentions famous people or brands only to borrow their credibility or attention.
descriptions.CREDENTIAL SIGNALING: Flaunts the creator's or guest's titles and degrees to justify a claim.
descriptions.PREDICTION AS FACT: States a prediction about the future as if it were settled.
descriptions.OPINION AS FACT: States an opinion as an objective truth.
descriptions.CORRELATION AS CAUSATION: Claims one thing causes another based only on them occurring together.
descriptions.ABSOLUTE CLAIM: Uses always, never, everyone, nobody or only, with no exceptions.
descriptions.CONTEXT OMISSION: Presents a fact while leaving out context that changes its meaning.
descriptions.OVERSIMPLIFICATION: Reduces a complicated issue to a single simple cause or answer.
descriptions.WEASEL WORDS: Uses phrases like 'some say' or 'reportedly' to avoid accountability.
descriptions.INSINUATION: Suggests something damaging without stating it.
descriptions.STRAW MAN: Attacks a weaker or distorted version of an opponent's position.
descriptions.LOADED QUESTION: Asks a question that presumes something unproven or damaging.
descriptions.RAGEBAIT: Deliberately provokes anger so the viewer clicks, argues or shares.
descriptions.OUTRAGE BAIT: Presents an event as an outrage the viewer is meant to react to.
descriptions.DRAMA BAIT: Promotes interpersonal conflict, feuds or gossip.
descriptions.CALLOUT BAIT: Names and criticizes a specific person or group in public.
descriptions.DUNKING: Mocks or humiliates someone for a mistake or bad take.
descriptions.US-VS-THEM: Splits the world into our group and an opposing group.
descriptions.SCAPEGOATING: Blames a specific group or person for a broader problem.
descriptions.IDENTITY APPEAL: Speaks to the viewer's identity (nation, religion, generation, profession) to get attention.
descriptions.CONSPIRACY FRAMING: Explains events as the result of a secret coordinated plot.
descriptions.HOPE BAIT: Offers a hopeful promise that is unlikely to come true.
descriptions.GET-RICH-QUICK: Promises large money in a short time with little effort.
descriptions.PASSIVE-INCOME PROMISE: Promises money that arrives without ongoing work.
descriptions.LOSS AVERSION: Frames what the viewer stands to lose rather than gain.
descriptions.SECRET FORMULA: Promises a secret step-by-step method that guarantees success.
descriptions.LIFE HACK: Promotes a clever trick that supposedly makes a task effortless.
descriptions.TRANSFORMATION PROMISE: Promises a dramatic personal change (body, income, skills, life).
descriptions.CALL TO ACTION: Explicitly tells the viewer to do something (buy, sign up, click, share).
descriptions.IMPERATIVE FRAMING: The title is phrased as a command ('Watch this', 'Stop doing that').
descriptions.COMMENT BAIT: Asks or dares viewers to comment.
descriptions.WATCH-TILL-THE-END: Promises something at the end of the video to keep viewers watching.
descriptions.SERIES BAIT: Signals a series or part number to hook viewers into more.
descriptions.DIRECT ADDRESS: Speaks directly to the viewer using 'you'.
descriptions.HOT TAKE: A deliberately provocative opinion meant to start arguments.
descriptions.MYTH-BUSTING: Claims to correct a widely held belief.
descriptions.COVER-UP FRAMING: Claims something is being covered up or hidden from the public.
descriptions.TESTIMONIAL: Uses a personal endorsement or first-hand recommendation as proof.
descriptions.CASE STUDY: Presents one example or experiment as evidence that a method works.
descriptions.SUCCESS STORY: Tells of someone succeeding to imply the viewer can too.
descriptions.USER COUNT: Cites how many people use or follow something.
descriptions.PARASOCIAL APPEAL: Presents the creator as the viewer's close friend.
descriptions.“NO BS” FRAMING: Claims to be straightforward and unlike other, dishonest sources.
descriptions.VULNERABILITY: Shares a personal struggle or emotion to build closeness.
descriptions.SPECTACLE: Sells visual or dramatic spectacle rather than information.
descriptions.EXTREME TEST: Pushes something to absurd limits as a test.
descriptions.STUNT: A risky or outlandish stunt done for attention.
descriptions.CHALLENGE: A formal or viral challenge someone completes.
descriptions.VERSUS FRAMING: Frames two things or people as opponents in a match.
descriptions.SCANDAL FRAMING: Frames a story as a scandal.
descriptions.COLLAPSE FRAMING: Frames a company, person or system as falling apart.
descriptions.PR FRAMING: Reads like a press release polishing an image.
descriptions.SALES PITCH: Directly pitches a product, course or service.
descriptions.ADVERTISEMENT DISGUISED AS CONTENT: An ad that is presented as ordinary content.
descriptions.MANUFACTURED CONTROVERSY: Stirs up a dispute where none really exists.
descriptions.QUOTE MINING: Pulls a short quote to make someone say something they did not mean.
descriptions.HEADLINE DISTORTION: The title says something different from what its subject actually said or did.
descriptions.SCIENCE-WASHING: Uses scientific-sounding language to make a weak claim look proven.
descriptions.AI-WASHING: Uses AI buzzwords to make something sound more advanced than it is.
descriptions.BELIEF VALIDATION: Tells viewers that what they already believe is right.
descriptions.ECHO-CHAMBER APPEAL: Targets one community's shared beliefs without challenging them.
descriptions.EDUCATIONAL: Plainly teaches or explains a topic.
descriptions.TUTORIAL: A how-to guide with no exaggerated promises.
descriptions.REVIEW: A straightforward evaluation of a product or work.
descriptions.UNCERTAIN: The title is too ambiguous to tell.
descriptions.INSUFFICIENT CONTEXT: Too short or cryptic to judge (for example a bare name or a single word).

deferred.reason: Cannot be judged from a title and channel name alone; revisit if later versions read thumbnails, transcripts or page metadata.
